items.text: Alexi Giannoulias has served as Illinois Secretary of State since January 2023. He previously served as Illinois Treasurer from 2007 to 2011 and chaired the Illinois Community College Board. He also served on the Chicago Public Library board of directors. As secretary, he launched a “Skip-The-Line” appointment system at DMV facilities and ended mandatory road tests for drivers ages 79 to 86.

sentences.text: Alexi Giannoulias has served as Illinois Secretary of State since January 2023.
He previously served as Illinois Treasurer from 2007 to 2011 and chaired the Illinois Community College Board.
He also served on the Chicago Public Library board of directors.
As secretary, he launched a “Skip-The-Line” appointment system at DMV facilities and ended mandatory road tests for drivers ages 79 to 86.

items.text: During his 2022 campaign, he proposed changing the state’s Automatic Voter Registration system to a back-end model that would add eligible voters to the rolls automatically. His campaign has proposed allowing 16- and 17-year-olds to pre-register so they are added to the rolls at 18. He supported a 2023 law making Illinois the first state to outlaw book bans. After a Texas sheriff accessed an Illinois license plate reader system to look for a woman who had an abortion, his office instructed the operating company to shut off access to out-of-state agencies. He supported a new law that establishes safety rules for e-bikes and scooters.

items.text: He announced the Illinois Reliable Information Sources program, a contract providing all residents access to a suite of digital research databases. He supported a law that prohibits the state and municipalities from suspending driver’s licenses for unpaid parking tickets.
